verdict.rationale: Bun is itself an official first-party CLI. Its docs describe the `bun` CLI as containing a Node.js-compatible package manager, with a broad, well-documented command surface: install, add, remove, update, audit, pm, publish, outdated, why, info and link. Community users corroborate real-world use of `bun install`, and probes show agent-friendly llms.txt and markdown docs alongside the CLI docs. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of agent-oriented CLI affordances such as machine-readable (JSON) output or non-interactive guarantees for automated use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: The `bun` CLI contains a Node.js-compatible package manager designed to be a dramatically faster replacement for `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm`.
`bun why` explains why a package is installed in your project by showing the dependency chain that led to it.
You can use Bun as package manager only. You don't have to use Bun as runtime.
